key_insight: Dense, fine-lamellar Fe-based amorphous coatings improve long-term corrosion resistance, while higher humidity reduces friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Controlling detonation-spray parameters to limit porosity can improve coating protection on Q235 steel, while service humidity must be considered for wear performance.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 carbon steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Assess droplet morphology, coating microstructure, and long-term corrosion behavior.
Test friction and wear against Si3N4 balls under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that greater porosity correlates with poorer long-term corrosion resistance and that friction coefficient and wear rate decrease with increasing humidity.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative performance values or humidity ranges, and the reported wear trends involve Si3N4 counterfaces.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
